request.instructions: You help one person decide what to do with one used item: keep it and fix it, reuse it in something, or sell or give it away. Write three cards from the facts given and the person's profile; never assume a part works when the tests do not say so, and never invent a fault the record does not hold. keep_fix: the likely problem or problems behind the recorded condition and faults (one entry 'works as it is' when nothing is wrong), the repair steps written for this person's level, the difficulty for this person (easy, moderate or hard) with a why that names the rated skill it rests on, the parts with a rough cost each, the total cost and the time; when the repair is not worth it for this person, say so with worth_fixing false and the why. reuse: two or three things to make of it that fit the person's skills and tools, each naming the other items they own that it would use (with_items; empty when none applies), the difficulty for this person and why, the extra parts with cost, and the time. sell: what makes it sellable as it stands, what listing and handing it over takes, and one note; give no price, the price guidance is a separate step. recommended: one of keep_fix, reuse, sell or give, with a one-line reason tied to the profile. Plain words, no hype; each list entry one line. Also: A card or a use rests only on items the person owns that fit it; when none fits, it lists the missing part under extra parts with its cost and never calls it one the person owns. Read the condition first: a part recorded as missing, bare or unpopulated is not working as it is, and a use of it says what must be added. Mistakes to avoid, found in earlier answers: Do not claim a use works without verifying assembly state and listing every required power supply, signal source, cable, and mating part as extra. Do not claim memory fits or can be tested without matching memory generation, per-slot limits, slot count, and a populated compatible socket with processor present. Do not claim a controller drives a monitor or sensor or input device without matching connectors, video or power interfaces, wiring needs, and intact mechanical parts. Do not propose storage, memory, or board use in a desktop without disclosing a missing compatible processor, power supply, or bootable host needed to run or test it. Never write these phrases or their like: "with the processor you own"; "your own processor".
